title: SLO governance workshare and comms manual (6-week cadence)
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines a lightweight, repeatable 6-week workshare and communications pattern for cross-functional SLO governance and reliability experiments. The goal is to create a predictable cadence so product, platform, SRE, and customer-facing teams can coordinate SLO changes, validation experiments, and runbook handoffs without ad-hoc firefighting.

Context and problem statement (quick):
- We have many localized SLO proposals that lack a shared validation plan and comms path.
- Product teams push SLO/threshold asks on different timelines -> inconsistent engineering capacity and surprise escalations.
- Runbooks and ownership are often implicit, not codified.
- Need a repeatable pattern that balances speed (fast experiments) with governance (risk-aware rollouts).

Principles (how we operate):
- Short feedback loops: small experiments (1–2 days) where possible; larger cohort validations across a week.
- Clear separation: \"who can change\" (owners) vs \"who must be notified\" (stakeholders).
- Shared artifacts: canonical SLO proposal + experiment plan stored in Confluence + tracking in Jira.
- Communication-first: designated announcement + escalation channel before any rollout.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- SLO proposal intake and triage
- 6-week sprint-like cadence for experiments and rollouts
- Roles & responsibilities (workshare matrix)
- Comms templates and channel patterns
- Measurement and stop/rollback rules
- Lightweight runbook handoffs

6-week cadence overview (high level):
- Week 0 (intake & triage): Proposals submitted, initial risk assessment, assign experiment owner.
- Week 1–2 (rapid micro-experiments): Small-scale validation (canary traffic, synthetic tests, KV-cache probes).
- Week 3 (analysis & decision): Collate metrics, decide canary->broader rollout or rollback.
- Week 4–5 (staggered rollouts / automation): Apply configuration changes to more capacity; enable observability dashboards.
- Week 6 (postmortem & stabilization): Runbook update, documentation, and retrospective; schedule next iteration if needed.

Detailed intake & triage process:
- Intake form fields (short): owner, service, current SLO, proposed SLO, user-impact rationale, traffic profile, risk level (low/med/high), linked PRs/tickets.
- Triage board: weekly SLO triage meeting (15–30m) with SRE lead, product lead, platform rep. Decisions: accept for 6-week cadence, defer, or reject.
- Quick risk flags: customer-impacting, billing impact, cross-region traffic shifts. If flagged, escalate to the reliability guardrail committee.

Workshare matrix (roles):
- Proposal owner (product / feature team): owns hypothesis, writes experiment plan, coordinates feature-side changes.
- SRE experiment lead: designs traffic shaping, controls canary ramp, defines telemetry to collect.
- Platform engineer: implements infra-level knobs (autoscale thresholds, batching configs) and supports rollback mechanisms.
- Observability owner: ensures dashboards/alerts are in place and that regression queries are written.
- CS/Support liaison: preps customer-facing comms if required and monitors incoming tickets.
- Reliability committee (monthly review): reviews high-risk proposals and approves exceptions.

Communication pattern and templates:
- Pre-intent announcement (Slack channel #ops-slo-intent): 48–72 hours before starting any canary. Minimal content: owner, service, what will change, expected window, rollback plan link.
- Canary kick notice (channel + email to stakeholders): at start of canary with link to live dashboard and oncall rotation.
- Mid-canary update (quick post): 24h summary if canary > 24h, otherwise immediate on anomalies.
- Closing report (Confluence + thread): includes metrics, decision rationale, and updated runbook link.
- Template examples (short):
  - Pre-intent: [owner] intends to change SLO for <service> from X->Y on <date>. Canary plan: <link>. Expected impact: <low|med|high>. Oncall: <rotation>.
  - Incident-rollback: if error rate > threshold OR latency degrade > X% for 3 consecutive minutes -> rollback to previous config and page SRE.

Measurement, SLIs, and stop conditions:
- Minimum required telemetry before canary: request success rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error subtypes, token-level cost (where applicable), and user-facing error counts.
- Stop/rollback rules (examples):
  - If SLI error-rate increases by more than 2x baseline for >5 minutes -> immediate rollback.
  - If tail latency (p99) increases 30% and correlates with user-visible errors -> pause rollout.
  - If cost-per-request increases >40% with no measurable UX improvement -> abort and investigate.
- Additional check: Ensure K-anomaly detectors show no systemic regressions across related services.

Experiment matrix (example rows):
- Hypothesis: \"Increasing request batch size reduces per-token cost without affecting p95 latency\"
  - Metric primary: per-token cost delta
  - Metric guard: p95 latency percent change
  - Canary traffic: 5% for 48h
  - Stop rule: p95 > +15% or errors +1.5x baseline

Runbook and handoff checklist (post-success):
- Update runbook: what changed, who owns monitoring, rollback steps (clear runbook section).
- Ownership handoff: assign primary and secondary SRE owners for first 30 days.
- Automation: add automated rollback via deployment pipeline if applicable.
- Documentation: link to Confluence SLO page and embed decision rationale + dashboards.

Meeting rhythm and artifacts:
- Triage standup (weekly, 20m): new proposals and quick blockers.
- SLO review (bi-weekly deep-dive, 60m): larger decisions requiring cross-team alignment.
- Reliability committee (monthly, 60m): high-risk decisions and policy updates.
- Artifacts: standard Confluence template for SLO proposal, Jira epic tag (RELIAB-SLO), Canary run notebook (shared Google Sheet).

Risk model and mitigation patterns:
- Risk: cascading latency increases due to shared infra.
  - Mitigation: start in a region with lowest traffic coupling; enable strict concurrency caps.
- Risk: customer-visible regression.
  - Mitigation: reduce canary audience to internal/test accounts, enable rapid egress to older model variant.
- Risk: cost spikes.
  - Mitigation: cost alerting and pre-declared budget threshold that triggers feature throttle.

Decision authority and exceptions:
- Low-risk changes: product + SRE experiment lead sign-off.
- Medium-risk: product + SRE + platform sign-off, notify reliability committee.
- High-risk (cross-region/customer SLA impact): require explicit reliability committee approval prior to canary.

Open questions / unresolved items (notes to self):
- How to record transient experiments that are intentionally ephemeral? Need tagging convention: slo-experiment:ephemeral.
- Do we need a shared synthetic traffic harness for consistent baselines? (cost vs benefit analysis required)
- Should CS be auto-notified only above medium-risk? Who owns customer opt-out list?

Practical templates (quick copy-paste):
- Canary pre-intent (Slack):
  \"[Maya Chen] intends to run a 48h canary to change SLO for auth-service from 99.9%->99.7% on 2026-03-08. Canary: 5% traffic, dashboard: <link>, rollback: <link>. If you have concerns, reply or page oncall@sre.\n- Postmortem header (Confluence):\n  Title: Canary outcome - <service> - <date>\n  Summary: one-paragraph decision + metrics snapshot\n  Actions: list + owners + due dates\n
Quick start checklist (for owners):
1) Fill intake form and attach PRs/tickets.
2) Present at triage; get slot in upcoming 6-week cadence.
3) Prep dashboard and alert query.
4) Run small internal test, then canary.
5) Follow comms pattern.
6) If successful, finalize runbook and close Jira epic.

Retrospective measures (success metrics):
- Time-to-decision: days between intake and canary start (target: <=14).
- Mean time to rollback (if happened): target < 30m for automated rollbacks, < 2h for manual.
- Percentage of SLO changes with documented runbooks: target 100%.
- Experiment signal quality: fraction of experiments with actionable metrics (target > 80%).

Next steps (action items):
- Iterate intake form (Maya) by 2026-03-10.
- Build a sample canary dashboard template (Observability team) by 2026-03-17.
- Pilot 2 SLO experiments using this cadence in March; retro on 2026-04-01.

Appendix — links & templates:
- Intake form: confluence:CI-RELIABILITY-SLO-GOV-345#intake-form
- Slack channels: #ops-slo-intent, #ops-slo-canary, #sre-incident
- Jira board: RELIAB-SLO (epic filter)

Notes: This doc is intentionally practical, not policy-heavy. The aim is to create a working pattern we can refine after two pilots. Expect many small edits — treat this as a living working doc.

Choppy notes / brainstorm fragments (drive-style):
- \"workshare\" = explicit tasks assigned for each triage slot (avoid implicit ownership)
- consider tagging canaries with experiment-id and owner for traceability
- need cheap synthetic harness -> maybe use canary-users pool or internal traffic mirrors
- followup: automation hooks to create rollback PRs automatically if thresholds tripped

End of document.
